scenario: The owner receives a duplicated reminder request while trying to set an alarm.

turns.text: Hey, can you set a reminder for me to take the laundry out at 3 PM?
Sure! I've set a reminder to take the laundry out at 3 PM.
duplicate webhook delivery of the user's reminder request.
I already have that reminder set, so no duplicate was created.

expected.agent_should: Ignore the duplicate delivery and only retain the original reminder.

scenario: A follow-up question is answered within a threaded conversation between the owner and the agent.

turns.text: @agent Can you look up a packing list for a weekend trip?
Sure! What kind of trip are you packing for, and about how many days?
Just a two day hiking trip!
Got it. Here's a simple two day hiking packing list: water, trail snacks, first-aid kit, rain shell, extra socks, headlamp, and a light tarp.

expected.agent_should: Keep all replies confined to the specified thread and answer the follow-up directly.

scenario: The agent is tasked with summarizing a large chunk of notes that were pasted in for a project update.

turns.text: @agent Can you summarize these notes for me: *Project Scope*: Build a light UI for internal testing. *Timeline*: Aim for an early review next month. *Blockers*: Waiting on access to a test inbox, example.com log previews need to be cleared, and the export script may need a small rewrite. *Priority*: Focus on accessibility fixes first. *Notes*: Reach out to the testing group for feedback before locking any changes.

Sure. Here's a quick summary: The top priority is accessibility fixes. You'll need to gain access to the test inbox, clear example.com log previews, and possibly rewrite the export script. Aim for an early review next month and get feedback from the testing group before locking changes.
Perfect, can you turn that into a one line status for a check in?
Working on accessibility first for the UI test build, with a few access blockers, targeting an early review next month.

expected.agent_should: Extract key points from the long message and provide a concise, accurate summary.

scenario: The owner quickly double checks an upcoming appointment with no complications.

turns.text: Hey, what time is my check-up tomorrow?
Your check-up is scheduled for 9:30 AM tomorrow.
Great, thank you!
You're very welcome!

expected.agent_should: Provide the correct appointment time and a polite follow-up.

scenario: A budget breakdown is calculated and referenced back in a thread after a duplicate delivery occurs.

turns.text: @agent Can we break down the grocery budget for this week in here?
Sure! How much are you looking to spend total this week for groceries?
$75 total.
With $75, you could allocate $50 for staples, $15 for produce, and $10 for extras.
duplicate webhook delivery of the budget allocation response context.
No changes needed, that allocation is still accurate for $75.

expected.agent_should: Ignore the duplicate webhook, keep the thread intact, and prevent any redundant budget recalculations.

scenario: The owner feeds a very detailed list of chores to the agent and asks for a prioritized schedule.

turns.text: @agent I need to tackle these chores this weekend: sweep the living room, take out all of the recycling, deep clean the fridge, water the backyard plants, wash the sheets, vacuum the stairs, clear out the small hallway closet, wipe down the kitchen appliances, take the bins to the curb for pickup, and do a quick tidy of the garage.

That is a solid list! With two days, I would prioritize: take out recycling and bins for curb pickup first (time sensitive), then deep clean the fridge, and vacuum the stairs for safety. From there, split the rest between Saturday afternoon and Sunday.
Nice, can you sort that into a Saturday and Sunday breakdown for me?

Saturday: curb pickup/recycling, deep clean the fridge, vacuum the stairs, and sweep the living room. Sunday: wash the sheets, water the backyard plants, clear the hallway closet, wipe down kitchen appliances, and do a quick tidy of the garage.

expected.agent_should: Parse the long list, prioritize time sensitive items, and split them into an actionable weekend plan.

scenario: An unrecognized user attempts to interact with the agent within a private Slack DM.

turns.text: Connector detected an incoming Slack DM from a non-allowlisted sender.
Hey, could you send me the notes from yesterday's meeting?
Connector rejected the request due to the sender not being on the allowlist.

expected.agent_should: Ignore the request and refrain from sending any replies to the non-allowlisted sender.

scenario: The owner cheers on a small task for the agent, utilizing a mix of Unicode and emojis.

turns.text: Good morning! ☀️ Could you please draft a grocery list for this week? 🛒
Sure! Here is a simple grocery list: Eggs, Milk, Bread, and Bananas. 🛍️
Perfect, you're a lifesaver! ✨
Glad to help! Let me know if you'd like to add anything else! 💚

expected.agent_should: Correctly parse Unicode and emojis whilst drafting and acknowledging the owner's follow-up.

scenario: The owner sends a flurry of quick commands to the agent in rapid succession.

turns.text: Set a reminder for 3 PM today.
Reminder set for 3 PM today.
Schedule a 5 minute break at 3:30 PM.
5 minute break scheduled for 3:30 PM.
Summarize today's top task.
Your top task for today is to review the pending draft over on example.com/review-drafts.

expected.agent_should: Process and reply to each of the rapid-fire commands in order without queue drops.

scenario: The owner has a straightforward follow-up conversation with the agent regarding a previously created reminder.

turns.text: Can you confirm if my water reminder is still active?
Yes, your water reminder is still active and is set to repeat every two hours.
Great, please keep it as is for now.
Noted. I will keep your water reminder unchanged.

expected.agent_should: Confirm the reminder's status and acknowledge the owner's request with a concise reply.

scenario: The owner continues a long-context discussion within a Slack thread and receives a duplicate delivery due to a provider retry.

turns.text: Starting a thread for a project summary. We need to recap feedback from three separate example.com/notes entries for our quarterly outline.
Got it. Pulling key points from the provided entries now.
Also, be sure to highlight action items that are still marked as pending, and avoid re-listing any that were closed in the previous sprint.
Duplicate webhook delivery of Slack event Ev0123ABCW received by connector due to Events API retry.
Summary draft complete. There are three pending action items: finalize assets, confirm availability, and review revisions. Closed items have been omitted.

expected.agent_should: Maintain thread context, generate a filtered summary, and safely ignore the duplicate delivery without sending an extra reply.

scenario: The owner rapidly asks for scheduling help across two tasks, testing the agent's ability to handle quick-fire requests.

turns.text: Find a free slot for a 15 minute check-in tomorrow.
I found an open slot tomorrow at 10:00 AM for your 15 minute check-in.
Also, can you block 20 minutes on Friday afternoon?
20 minutes has been blocked for Friday afternoon on your calendar.

expected.agent_should: Respond to both rapid-fire scheduling requests accurately and in sequence.

scenario: Morgan needs the agent to piece together a reminder request after Slack events arrive out of order.

turns.text: @agent can you remind me to grab the sample bins tomorrow morning?
@agent actually make that around 8:45 AM instead.
Got it. I'll remind you tomorrow at 8:45 AM to grab the sample bins.
Connector re-ordered events by received_at to preserve conversation timeline due to out_of_order delivery.

expected.agent_should: Reconstruct the latest reminder intent from out-of-order thread messages and confirm a single reminder with the corrected time.

scenario: Jordan sends only a media attachment with no text and expects the agent to ask for context safely.

turns.text: [image attachment: chart_example.png]
I can see an attachment, but I don't have any description for it. Could you tell me what you'd like me to do with this chart?
Pull the totals from the Q2 column for me.
Based on your note, I'll extract the Q2 totals from that chart and summarize them in a short reply.

expected.agent_should: Treat a media_only Slack message as incomplete, prompt for clarification before taking action, then answer the follow-up.

scenario: Cameron asks the agent to send a message to an external distro list and the connector requires an approval step first.

turns.text: @agent please blast the update to distro@example.com about the maintenance window for +15551230001 recipients.
This action would send an outbound message to distro@example.com. Do you approve sending this maintenance update? Reply with 'approve' to continue.
approve
Approved. I've queued the maintenance window update for distro@example.com with the requested details.

expected.agent_should: Issue an explicit approval_prompt before any outbound send action, wait for owner confirmation, then execute only after approval.

scenario: Morgan has a quick, self-contained question about a local checklist with no unusual edge cases.

turns.text: @agent do I still have any open checklist items for the setup run?
You have 2 open checklist items for the setup run: 'verify power cables' and 'test backup access'.
Mark 'verify power cables' as done.
Done. 'Verify power cables' is now marked complete. 1 item still open: 'test backup access'.

expected.agent_should: Answer the checklist query accurately and apply the update requested, keeping replies concise.

scenario: Jordan is following up across a thread while two earlier webhook deliveries for the same message arrive late and out of order.

turns.text: @agent summarize the action items from today's sync notes.
duplicate webhook delivery of Slack event: same provider_message_id detected.
Also include who's following up for each one.
Action items from today's sync: 1) Update access docs – follow-up by Jordan (example.com request), 2) Verify test endpoints – follow-up by Cameron, 3) Confirm backup window – follow-up by Morgan.
Thanks, export that as a one-line recap for +15551234444 context.
Recap: access docs (Jordan), test endpoints (Cameron), backup window (Morgan) – all pending follow-ups.

expected.agent_should: Ignore the duplicate_delivery, correctly order thread turns despite out_of_order timestamps, and provide a single, deduplicated summary with the requested one-line recap.

scenario: Cameron requests a sensitive schedule change that requires approval before committing updates to the shared calendar.

turns.text: @agent move all upcoming check-ins for the onboarding batch starting next week to +1 hour later, update every occurrence through the end of the month, and notify each participant at their listed example.com contact where applicable.

This is a bulk calendar change affecting multiple recurring check-ins through the end of the month. Approve rescheduling all of those occurrences by +1 hour and sending participant notifications? Reply 'approve' to confirm.
approve
Approved. I've rescheduled all onboarding batch check-ins for next week onward through month-end to +1 hour later and queued notifications to the listed example.com contacts.

expected.agent_should: Require explicit approval_prompt for a high-scope, long_context bulk calendar operation and only apply changes after confirmation.

scenario: The connector encounters a temporary provider error and must retry delivery before the agent responds.

turns.text: Hey agent, can you set a reminder for me to water the plants at 5 PM today?
Slack Events API returned a transient provider error while attempting to process incoming message.
Connector retried webhook delivery and successfully reprocessed the original event.
Got it, Jordan. I'll remind you to water the plants at 5 PM today.

expected.agent_should: Retry the failed event without creating a duplicate user request and send one confirmation reply.

scenario: The owner makes an ambiguous request and the agent needs to clarify before taking action.

turns.text: Agent, move that thing to later.
Hey Morgan, could you clarify what you'd like me to move to later? For example, a reminder, meeting, or task?
The reminder about picking up supplies.
Got it. I've rescheduled the 'pick up supplies' reminder to a later time slot as requested.

expected.agent_should: Ask for clarification on an ambiguous instruction instead of guessing, then proceed after the follow-up.

scenario: A duplicate webhook delivery is received for an existing request and must be ignored.

turns.text: Agent, can you give me a quick summary of my notes from today?
Sure, Casey. Your notes for today show one follow-up for +15551234567 and one draft sent to alex@example.com.
duplicate webhook delivery of Slack event detected.
Thanks, that's all for now.
You're welcome, Casey. Let me know if you need anything else!

expected.agent_should: Process the original request once, drop the duplicate delivery, and only respond to unique user turns.

scenario: A threaded conversation has a duplicate delivery mid-thread that should not interrupt the context.

turns.text: @agent Let's brainstorm ideas for a small project in this thread.
Sounds good, Riley. What kind of project are we thinking of?
Something simple that can be tracked in a checklist.
duplicate webhook delivery of Slack event detected within thread.
Nice idea, Riley. I can create a checklist with tasks and check off items as we go.

expected.agent_should: Maintain thread context, ignore the duplicate thread message, and reply only to the unique user input.

scenario: Multiple connector retries occur due to provider errors before the agent can complete a scheduling request.

turns.text: Agent, can you schedule a quick check-in with me for Friday at 2 PM?
Slack Events API returned a transient provider error while queuing the incoming request.
Connector performed a retry attempt for the original webhook event.
All set, Cameron. I've scheduled your quick check-in for Friday at 2 PM.

expected.agent_should: Safely retry on provider errors, avoid re-executing the action from duplicates, and send exactly one confirmation.

scenario: An owner asks a general follow-up with no specifics, requiring clarification with no connector failures present.

turns.text: Agent, can you follow up on that?
Hey Drew, which item would you like me to follow up on? You can tell me the reminder, message, or task name.
Follow up on the reminder sent to +15557654321 about the sample pickup.
Done, Drew. I've queued a follow-up for the sample pickup reminder sent to +15557654321.

expected.agent_should: Politely clarify the vague request and only execute once concrete details are provided.

scenario: Tracking action items by continuing a discussion inside of an existing Slack thread.

turns.text: @assistant Could we check on the status of the outline for the notes packet?
The outline is still in review. I can ping the editor once it's assigned.
Great, please hold a copy for me and flag anything that needs trimming.
I'll keep a draft copy aside and flag any text over the target length.
Perfect. If the word count drops below half, let me know in this thread as well.
Noted. I'll update you here if that threshold is reached.

expected.agent_should: Respond to all follow-ups within the specified thread without starting a new DM.

scenario: Processing a large block of context to generate a compact summary for later reference.

turns.text: @assistant Please summarize the following for a recap: We need to onboard two new readers, assign a backup cover for Thursdays, verify access to the example.com archive, confirm receipt templates, track feedback over the next five weeks, and log any blockers in the shared notes. Prioritize blockers first.

Blockers: backup cover for Thursdays (unconfirmed), access to the example.com archive (pending). Others: onboarding two readers (in queue), receipt templates (to review), five-week feedback window (track), shared notes logging (routine).
Can you expand on the backup cover, listing at least two possible swaps without losing coverage for early slots?

Swap one: move the early Thursday slot to the first reserve for that week. Swap two: shift a mid-week make-up slot to cover the early block and offset later. Both would require approval from a cover lead.
Pick one concrete action for me to take today, keeping in mind the limited time.
Action today: contact the first reserve about covering the early Thursday block and ask for a yes or no by the end of the day.

expected.agent_should: Condense the long context into a structured summary and give a single, actionable next step.

scenario: Rejecting messages from a non-allowlisted sender while still protecting the owner's inbox.

turns.text: Message received from an unrecognized Slack account attempting to @mention the agent.
I can only respond to authorized senders for this assistant. This message will not be processed.
@assistant Ignore that, I am the owner. Can you reschedule my pickup for tomorrow afternoon?
Sure. What time window works best for a tomorrow afternoon pickup?
Between two and four in the afternoon would be ideal.
I've noted the pickup for tomorrow between 14:00 and 16:00.

expected.agent_should: Block unrecognized senders and resume normal operation for the allowlisted owner.

scenario: Handling a duplicate webhook delivery for a reminder request without sending a double reply.

turns.text: Incoming webhook delivery for a Slack message.
@assistant Set a quick reminder for me to call +15551234001 at five o'clock today.
Reminder set: call +15551234001 at 17:00 today.
duplicate webhook delivery of Slack message with provider_message_id Ev0123BA09.
Also, please include a short note: 'check parking'.
Added the note 'check parking' to that reminder.

expected.agent_should: Deduplicate the event and only reply once for the original request.

scenario: Navigating a short follow-up while respecting an opt-out and a later opt-in to resume messaging.

turns.text: @assistant Send me the weekly digest from example.com/weekly to me at the owner inbox? Actually, opt me out for now.
carrier opt-out confirmation sent for the owner's Slack delivery preferences.
Opt-out processed. I will stop sending automated digests until you opt back in.
Never mind, opt me back in. I'd still like a brief version of today's digest.
opt-in resume recorded for the owner's Slack delivery preferences.
Opt-in recorded. Here's a brief digest: no major blockers, one small edit queued.

expected.agent_should: Honor opt-out and opt-in resume before delivering messages.

scenario: Tackling a mixed set of queries with emoji, follow-ups and rapid-fire clarification without losing focus.

turns.text: @assistant help — I need to sort files ✨ for three projects today.
Happy to help. Which three projects should I sort by priority?
First, notes. Second, receipts. Third, drafts.
Priority order set: notes → receipts → drafts.
Keep only items from this month for receipts, but keep all drafts for now.
Filters applied: receipts limited to this month; drafts kept in full.
👍 One last thing — show me how many will be left at the end.
Estimated final count: notes (8), receipts (5), drafts (12). Total 25.

expected.agent_should: Parse rapid-fire requests accurately, including unicode_emoji and a help_keyword, and provide a final summary.

scenario: The owner gets in a groggy mood and uses a large amount of emojis to set their morning reminder.

turns.text: Gooood morningggg ☀️😴, can you please set a reminder for me to feed Milo the cat at 8 AM?
Sure thing! I've scheduled a reminder to feed Milo the cat at 8:00 a.m. today. 🐈
You're an absolute lifesaver 🥰!!!
Happy to help! I'll ping you at 8:00 a.m. as requested.

expected.agent_should: Set the cat feeding reminder and respond in a friendly manner while preserving the owner's tone.

scenario: In the midst of a busy work block, the owner fires off a string of rapid fire questions to the agent.

turns.text: What's the weather looking like for tomorrow?
Can you add 'water the plants' to my afternoon list?
Looks clear and sunny tomorrow! I've also added 'water the plants' to your afternoon task list.
Do we still have grocery eggs?
According to your shopping notes, you're still stocked up on eggs! Let me know if you'd like anything else.

expected.agent_should: Batch and accurately answer each of the rapid fire queries without dropping any of them.

scenario: Due to a network retry, the connector receives messages out of order while scheduling a follow up meeting.

turns.text: Can you schedule a five minute check in for Friday afternoon?
Sure, I've blocked off five minutes on Friday afternoon for a check in. What time would you prefer?
Actually, nevermind, make it Thursday at noon instead.
Noted, I've rescheduled your check in to Thursday at noon instead. All set!

expected.agent_should: Reorder the context correctly and treat the latest intent as correct, overriding the earlier request.

scenario: The owner takes a moment to politely request a short summary for their notes in a DM.

turns.text: Morning! Could you give me a quick summary of the bullet points that I jotted down yesterday?
Of course! Here is a quick recap: finalize the draft, send over a review to the team, and check for feedback by the end of the day.
That looks perfect, thank you!
You're welcome! Let me know if you'd like to expand on any of those points.

expected.agent_should: Provide an accurate, concise summary and close the exchange politely.

scenario: The owner and the agent continue a long running thread, getting distracted with a few emojis in between tasks.

turns.text: @agent Can we pick back up on the onboarding list for a new hire?
Sure, we're back in this thread! The next item on the list is to assign their laptop login credentials. Shall I queue that up?
Yes, and maybe throw in a welcome pack too! 🎉
Done! The laptop credentials and welcome pack have both been queued for setup. 🚀

expected.agent_should: Keep all replies scoped to the specified thread and correctly carry out the queued actions.

scenario: After a webhook retry, a duplicate delivery causes a system event whilst the owner is setting a last minute reminder.

turns.text: Ah shoot, I need a reminder in five minutes to take the cookies out of the oven!
Got it, I've set a reminder to take the cookies out of the oven in five minutes.
duplicate webhook delivery of Ev0123ABCJ1 detected; ignoring to prevent a double response.
No need to rush, I'll be sure to ping you right on time!

expected.agent_should: Acknowledge the valid request, discard the duplicate delivery, and only send replies for new content.

scenario: Jordan wants the agent to interpret an image that was sent with no caption.

turns.text: I don't see any text attached to this image. Could you tell me what you'd like me to do with it?
It's a quick grocery list for later.
Got it. I'll save your grocery list for you to reference later.

expected.agent_should: Ask for context when only media is provided before taking action.

scenario: Morgan needs the agent to delete a shared reminder, but the action requires approval first.

turns.text: Can you delete the reminder I set for +15551230001 at example.com?
This action will permanently delete that reminder. Do you want me to proceed?
Yes, go ahead and delete it.
Done. The reminder has been deleted.

expected.agent_should: Request explicit approval before performing a destructive action and only execute after confirmation.

scenario: Cameron is asking for a follow-up while the connector encounters a temporary provider error and retries the request.

turns.text: Can you summarize the notes I left for today?
provider error: Slack webhook delivery timed out while processing inbound event. Retrying event delivery.
duplicate webhook delivery of Slack event due to provider retry.
Summary: You have two follow-ups to check, one reminder for later today, and a draft reply to finish.

expected.agent_should: Retry safely without sending duplicate replies when receiving a retried provider event.

scenario: Jordan is continuing a task inside a thread, sending only an image as their response.

turns.text: @agent Pull the items from this receipt when you get it.
Sure, send the receipt in this thread and I'll extract the items.
I can see the receipt. I've pulled five items and added them to your notes.

expected.agent_should: Keep the entire exchange within the specified thread and interpret media-only replies in that context.
